chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid from Abu Jamilyah from Abu Usamah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the Takbir (saying Allahu Akbar) during the two Eids, he said seven and five, and he said: 'The prayer of the two Eids is obligatory, and the prayer of the eclipse is obligatory.'

key_terms.التَّكْبِيرِ: The act of saying 'Allahu Akbar' (God is the Greatest), often used in the context of prayer invocations.
key_terms.الْعِيدَيْنِ: The two Eids, referring to Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha.
key_terms.الْكُسُوفِ: The solar or lunar eclipse, specifically referring to the special prayer performed during an eclipse.
key_terms.فَرِيضَةٌ: Obligatory or mandatory duty in Islamic jurisprudence.

ai.seo_question: How many Takbirat are recited in Eid prayers and are they obligatory?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies the number of Takbirat in Eid prayers and explicitly classifies both Eid and Eclipse prayers as obligatory (fard), a ruling that distinguishes the Shia view from the Hanafi school which considers them sunnah mu'akkadah. The hadith is recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, highlighting the jurisprudential authority of the Imams in defining ritual obligations. This establishes a clear legal precedent for the performance of these specific congregational prayers within Shia fiqh.
